answers.a: Predict whether a newly placed order will be returned using only information available at order placement, and identify associated factors.
Returns consume logistics cost after checkout. A probability at placement is early enough to review high-risk orders without waiting for shipment data.
Returned vs not returned is the operational decision unit. The business action (review, outreach) is at order level, so the label is order-level.
The moment the customer places the order. Profit, shipping cost, ship date, return date, and return reason are excluded.

Duplicate order_id rows that counted an order as its own history were dropped. Customer history uses only earlier orders (date, then order_id). The 2021 test set was not used for model selection or threshold tuning.

Current-order fields (value, quantity, discount, segment, region, priority, calendar) plus point-in-time history (prior orders, prior returns, historical return rate, average prior order value, days since previous order).

answers.q: Why the statistical test was selected
answers.a: The research question is a comparison of two proportions. A two-sided two-proportion z-test matches that question. Result: z=0.54, p=0.5887. Significance is not causation.

answers.q: Why these ML models were selected
answers.a: A majority baseline shows the imbalance. Logistic regression is a linear, inspectable model. Random forest and XGBoost capture non-linear interactions. The set is small on purpose.

answers.q: Why the final model was selected
answers.a: Validation PR-AUC (2020), not a pre-chosen algorithm. Comparison: Majority-class baseline: PR-AUC 0.059, ROC-AUC 0.500; Logistic Regression: PR-AUC 0.148, ROC-AUC 0.630; Random Forest: PR-AUC 0.118, ROC-AUC 0.674; XGBoost: PR-AUC 0.090, ROC-AUC 0.631. Selected: Logistic Regression.
On the untouched 2021 test set: ROC-AUC 0.693, PR-AUC 0.154, precision 0.175, recall 0.343, F1 0.232, accuracy 0.858 (secondary), Brier 0.170.
Overall return rate is 5.9%. Accuracy is easy to inflate by always predicting no return. PR-AUC focuses on ranking the positive class.
Threshold 0.65 was chosen to maximize F1 on validation, then locked. The test set was not used to pick it.

SHAP attributes how features move a prediction up or down versus a baseline. It is not causal. Top global |SHAP| features (validation sample): num__number_of_products, num__previous_return_count, cat__region_West, num__max_discount, num__quantity.
West had the highest observed regional return rate (11.7%, n=1,611) versus South (2.9%, n=822).

The model can flag higher-risk orders at placement for targeted review or customer-experience follow-up. It should not be used to automatically block customers. Any operational intervention (holds, outreach, policy changes) would need a controlled experiment / A/B test to estimate causal impact on return rate or cost. This project does not claim a percentage reduction in returns.

Labeled data is US Superstore orders 2018-01-03 to 2021-12-30 (5,009 orders). Product category is not in the labeled table. Train 2,007 / val 1,315 / test 1,687. TimeSeriesSplit mean PR-AUC on train folds: 0.10050344697265316. No experiment measures causal return reduction. India is not in this labeled table.
